statement: A collateral attack on the validity of a grant can be mounted by raising an issue in defence, but the defendant must establish that defence by proving the invalidity of the grant.
supporting_quote: The general principle is that any defect that would be treated as jurisdictional in direct proceedings is equally available in a collateral challenge.

statement: A trust may be created for any lawful purpose, and the unlawful purposes that would forbid a trust being created are specifically referred to in section 4(1) of the Trusts Ordinance.
supporting_quote: Section 4(1) of the Trusts Ordinance as stated earlier clearly refers to the fact that a trust may be created for any lawful purpose. The unlawful purposes, which would forbid a Trust being created, are specifically referred to in section 4(1).

statement: A subsequent owner who buys over the head of a tenant can get the benefit of section 2(4)(c) of the Rent Act No 55 of 1980, even if they did not occupy the premises on 1st January 1980, as long as the original owner was in occupation of the premises on that date and let the premises to the tenant after that date.
supporting_quote: Therefore it is abundantly clear that the plaintiff is not estopped from having recourse to the exceptions as laid down in section 2(4)(c) of the Amendment to the Rent Act No 55 of 1980.

statement: Where the extent of a grant of land is stated in an ambiguous manner in a conveyance, it is legitimate to look at the conveyance in the light of the circumstances which surrounded it in order to ascertain what was therein expressed as the intention of the parties.
supporting_quote: Where the extent of a grant of land is stated in an ambiguous manner in a conveyance, it is legitimate to look at the conveyance in the light of the circumstances which surrounded it in order to ascertain what was therein expressed as the intention of the parties.

statement: It is not mandatory to read the documents in evidence at the conclusion of the trial, but if the opposing party does not object, the documents are deemed to be good evidence for all purposes of the law.
supporting_quote: It has been held that this is the cursus curiae of the original courts. See, Silva v. Kindersle [18 NLR 65]; Adaicappa Chettiar v. Thomas Cook and Son [31 NLR 385], Perera v. Seyed Mohomed [58 NLR 246]; Balapitiya Gunananda Thero v. Talalle Methananda Thero [(1997) 2 Sri LR 101]; Cinemas Limited v. Sounderarajan [(1988) 2 Sri LR 16]; Stassen Exports Ltd., v. Brooke Bond Group Ltd., and Two others [(2010) BLR 249].

statement: A right of way by prescription for a 3 feet wide road can be established through necessity and user for over ten years.
supporting_quote: I observe that the Appellant had proved a right of way by prescription for a 3 feet wide road over 10 years.

statement: A possessory action can be filed if the plaintiff is disturbed but not ousted from the land in their occupation.
supporting_quote: Disturbance of possession was protected by the mandament van maintenue. The applicant for such a relief had to give a concise account of his possession and of the disturbance caused by the other party.

statement: A permit issued on the prescribed form will be the primary evidence by which the fact of a permit may be proved.
supporting_quote: A permit issued on the prescribed form will be the primary evidence by which this fact may be proved.

statement: The right of pre-emption applies only when the property proposed to be sold is an undivided share.
supporting_quote: The right of pre-emption shall not be exercised except in a case where the property which is to be sold consists of an undivided share and interest in immovable property, and shall in no case be permitted where such property is held in sole ownership by the intending vendor

statement: In a rei vindicatio action, the plaintiff must establish that he is the owner of the property.
supporting_quote: In the case of D.A.Wanigaratne Vs Juwanis Appuhamy 65 NLR 167 wherein this court held that in action rei vindication the plaintiff must prove and establish his title.

statement: A party cannot put forward a ground of appeal for the first time in appeal unless it might have been put forward in the Court below and the matter in question should be a pure question of law.
supporting_quote: Accordingly the Appellate Court could consider a point raised for the first time in appeal, if the following requirements are fulfilled. a. the question raised for the first time in appeal, is a pure question of law and is not a mixed question of law and fact; b. the question raised for the first time in appeal is an issue put forward in the Court below under one of the issues raised; and c. the Court which hears the appeal has before it all the material that is required to decide the question.

statement: A co-owner can eject a trespasser from the co-owned property without joining the other co-owners as parties to the suit.
supporting_quote: even a co-owner has every right to eject the trespassers without making other co-owners parties to the suit.

statement: A tenant must expressly attorn to the new landlord and continue to pay rent to the transferee from the day of the receipt of the notice of the new transfer, if they want to keep the contract of tenancy.
supporting_quote: The tenant has to expressly attorn to the new landlord and continue to pay the rent to the transferee from the day of the receipt of the notice of the new transfer, if he wants to keep the contract of tenancy.

statement: When the Plaintiffs claiming as Trustees institute an action to safeguard or assert rights to the Trust property and the question at issue is whether the title to the Trust property is vested in the Plaintiffs or in the Defendants, the Plaintiffs are not entitled to maintain the action without first obtaining a vesting order under Section 112 of the Trusts Ordinance.
supporting_quote: When the Plaintiffs claiming as Trustees institute an action to safeguard or assert rights to the Trust property and the question at issue is whether the title to the Trust property is vested in the Plaintiffs or in the Defendants, the Plaintiffs are not entitled to maintain the action without first obtaining a vesting order under Section 112 of the Trusts Ordinance.

statement: In a rei vindicatio action, the plaintiff must prove and establish his title.
supporting_quote: The plaintiff must prove and establish his title.

statement: A tenant is entitled to a full or partial refund of rent in cases where a vis major or casus fortuitus has prevented him from using the property for the purposes for which it was leased, either completely or to a significant extent.
supporting_quote: The Appellants are thus entitled to the relief claimed. Page 20 of 20 I set aside the judgment of the High Court dated 25th May 2016 and affirm the judgment of the District Court dated 27th July 2012. The learned District Judge of Matara is directed to enter decree accordingly. Appeal allowed. Parties shall bear their costs.

statement: A plaintiff must show the grounds on which they seek exemption from the operation of the law of limitation.
supporting_quote: the rule in Section 44 is mandatory and therefore whenever a Plaintiff seeks exemption from the operation of the law of limitation, he must show the grounds on which he seeks such exemption – see Don Palis Appuhamy v. Perera2.

statement: A constructive trust is not created if the deed of transfer does not indicate an intention to create a constructive trust or that any such information was furnished on the Notary.
supporting_quote: In addition it was not evident from the said Deed, P1, that the money paid by the Respondent was a loan. The Appellant states that she had repaid the said sum with interest, however when asked why she didn't take steps to get a re-transfer of the property she was unable to provide a justifiable answer.

statement: The word 'Adhikari' is a synonym for the word 'Viharadhipathi'.
supporting_quote: He had come to the conclusion that adhikari and viharadhipathi are synonymous terms.

statement: A co-owner should be allotted the portion which contains his improvements so far as is practicable.
supporting_quote: Whenever possible, co-owners should be allotted the portions containing their improvements. A co-owner is not entitled as of right to be allotted the portion containing his improvements.

statement: A deed's description of land is conclusive as defined and distinctive land, unless it lacks sufficient details to enable identification of the land.
supporting_quote: Relying on this interpretation it is the finding of this Court that the description of a land in a deed is conclusive as defined and distinctive land.

statement: A final land settlement order made and duly published in the Government Gazette is conclusive proof of the title of the persons in whose favour it was made.
supporting_quote: Subject to the provisions of section 5(6), every settlement order shall be published in the Gazette, and every settlement order so published shall be judicially noticed and shall be conclusive proof, so far as the State or any person is thereby declared to be entitled to any land or to any share of or interest in any land, that the State or such person is entitled to such land or to such share of or interest in the land or to such share of or interest in the land free of all encumbrances whatsoever other than those specified in such order and that subject to the encumbrance specified in such order such land or share or interest vests absolutely in the State or in such person to the exclusion of all unspecified interests of whatsoever nature and, so far as it is thereby declared that any land is not claimed by the State or that some person unascertained is entitled to a particular share of or interest in any land, that the State has no title to such land or that some person unascertained is entitled to such share of the land or that such interest in the land exists and that some person unascertained is entitled thereto, as the case maybe: Provided that nothing in this section contained shall affect the right of any person prejudiced by fraud or the willful suppression of facts of any claimant under the notice from proceedings against such claimant either for the recovery of damages or for the recovery of the land awarded to such claimant by the order.

statement: To establish prescriptive acquisition of immovable property, a defendant must prove undisturbed and uninterrupted possession for more than 10 years.
supporting_quote: Proof of the undisturbed and uninterrupted possession by a defendant in any action, or by those under whom he claims, of lands or immovable property, by a title adverse to or independent of that of the claimant or plaintiff in such action (that is to say, a possession unaccompanied by payment of rent or produce, or performance of service or duty, or by any other act by the possessor, from which an acknowledgment of a right existing in another person would fairly and naturally be inferred) for ten years previous to the bringing of such action, shall entitle the defendant to a decree in his favour with costs.

statement: A party is bound to take steps and proceed with all possible and reasonable expedition to prosecute an action without allowing it to accumulate on the case list.
supporting_quote: People may do what they like with their disputes as long as they do not invoke the assistance of the Courts of Law. But whenever that step has been taken they are bound to proceed with all possible and reasonable expedition, and it is the duty of their legal advisors and of the Courts themselves to seek that this is done.

statement: A court commissioner's plan can be used to identify the encroachment of an access road by a defendant.
supporting_quote: The surveyor Gunasiri Mendis had superimposed Plan No. 164 relied on by the Plaintiffs and Plan No. 1178 containing Lots 32 and 33 within that area which is relied on by the Defendants, on the total area surveyed by him and identified that the Defendants had encroached on the access road.
